body: Actual: +0.3% MoM vs +0.4% forecast (previous +1.4%, revised); +6.5% YoY vs +6.6% forecast. Core +0.3% MoM, in line.

What it means: the monthly number cooled, but the yearly number is still hot — +6.5% YoY is the biggest annual rise since November 2022, and core is +4.9% YoY. With a December Fed hike still priced and Treasury yields above 5%, the pressure on gold has paused, not lifted.

Gold's reaction (Kitco): spot caught a modest bid to about $3,897.90, +0.57% on the day, testing resistance at $3,900 — a bounce off Thursday's 52-week low near $3,852 after a three-session fall of about 6%.
Levels: a firm hold above $3,900 opens $3,930, then $3,950–$3,970 and $4,000. If the bounce fails, $3,870 and then the $3,852 low are exposed again.
Call: NO TRADE into the bounce — the desk's standing rule held (no manual scalps 20:15–21:30 Phnom Penh on release night). Reassess once gold either holds above $3,900 or loses $3,870.
headline: PPI cooler than expected — a relief bounce for gold, not a trend change
Logan speaks in ~10 min — hawkish stance already priced in, no trade into the speech
body: No forecast — a speech, not data. Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan (2026 FOMC voter) gives opening remarks at the 2026 Bank Funding Conference.

Her stance is already known and priced in: on Tuesday she said the FOMC needs 'at least two more 25bp hikes' and the rate is ~50bp below modestly restrictive. Gold has already fallen 4%+ this week on this hawkish repricing, with the dollar at a 19-month high.
Gold ~$3,890, just under $3,900, day range ~$3,873–3,923, just above its 52-week low near $3,853. A hawkish repeat keeps it capped under $3,900.
Tonight's PPI came in a touch softer than forecast (0.3% vs 0.4% MoM) and gave gold a small bounce — but core stayed sticky, so the Fed's hawkish line hasn't cracked.
Flip: a dovish softening (pause talk) would turn it BUY toward $3,900–3,923; a 50bp December hike endorsement would turn it SELL, watch $3,873 then $3,853.
Caution: the first minutes after any headline are spike territory — no manual scalps into the speech, per the standing rule.

headline: Logan's speech was technical — no new rate signal, hawkish backdrop unchanged
body: What she said: at the Dallas Fed's Bank Funding Conference, Logan said the US Treasury market is functioning 'very well' and the Fed should strengthen its support tools, including extending discount-window operations to weekends and holidays.

No new rate-path signal: her Tuesday stance (at least two more 25bp hikes) stands unchanged. The hawkish backdrop is intact — December hike ~89–91% priced, dollar near a 19-month high, 10-year yield ~5.13%.

Gold ~$3,890–3,910, recovering modestly from Thursday's 13-month low (~$3,874) but still under the $3,900–3,910 pivot and on track for a >4% weekly loss. No source reports a specific gold move on the speech.
Levels: resistance $3,925 / $3,937 above; support $3,884 / $3,875 / $3,860 below. A break of $3,937 would change the picture.
Call: NO TRADE — nothing tradable in a technical speech, and Bowman speaks at 22:50 Phnom Penh with Daly at 00:00. No manual scalps into those prints, per the standing rule.

headline: Bowman speaks in ~13 min — same hawkish message as Tuesday, low surprise value
body: No forecast — a speech, not data. Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman speaks at 22:50 Phnom Penh.

Her last remarks were Tuesday (10 Nov) at the Council on Foreign Relations: inflation 'has persisted longer than hoped', 'still work to do' to reach 2%, core PCE ~3.3% — a hawkish lean, but she stopped short of endorsing a December hike. Tonight likely echoes that.
Gold ~$3,888–3,891, recovering slightly after Thursday's ~3% slide to a 13-month low, but still down ~4% this week. Support $3,853–3,870, resistance $3,937.
Backdrop stays hawkish: a December 25bp hike is ~85–89% priced and the dollar is near a 19-month high; today's PPI came in a touch soft (MoM 0.3% vs 0.4% forecast), giving gold only a small lift.
Flip: an explicit December hike or 50bp endorsement would turn it SELL (dollar up, gold down); a softening — hikes off the table or inflation easing — would turn it BUY.
Caution: the first minutes after a Fed speech headline are spike territory — no manual scalps into the print, per the standing rule.

headline: Bowman's speech was on supervision and regulation — no new rate signal, hawkish backdrop unchanged
body: What she said: tonight's speech was on supervision and regulation (per the Fed schedule), not the economy or rates — in line with her role as Vice Chair for Supervision. No new rate-path remarks have been reported in the wires.

Her stance is unchanged from Tuesday (10 Nov): inflation 'has persisted longer than hoped', 'still work to do' to reach 2%, core PCE ~3.3% — a hawkish lean, but she stopped short of endorsing a December hike.

What it means for gold: nothing changes. The hawkish backdrop is intact — a December 25bp hike is ~88% priced, the 10-year yield is ~5.13%, and the dollar is near a 19-month high. No source reports a gold move on the speech.
Gold ~$3,878, drifting just under $3,900 after today's small PPI bounce, still down ~4% on the week after Thursday's slide to a 13-month low near $3,853.
Levels: resistance $3,900 / $3,937 above; support $3,870 / $3,853 below. Next up: Fed's Daly speaks at 00:00 Phnom Penh — no manual scalps into that print, per the standing rule.
Call: NO TRADE — a supervision speech with no policy content is not tradable for gold.

event: Fed Chair Warsh Opening Remarks (AI forum, San Francisco)
headline: Warsh speaks in ~10 min — themed AI remarks, little direct policy signal expected
body: No forecast — a speech, not data. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh opens the Fed's Productivity and Jobs Task Force conference in San Francisco, on whether AI will lower inflation, raise prices, or displace workers.
Opening remarks at a themed conference usually carry little direct policy guidance — and Warsh has said he doesn't prejudge meetings and avoids forward guidance.
Gold ~$3,863, down ~0.6% today, pinned just above $3,850 support after a ~4.5% drop last week to a 13-month low ($3,832 overnight). Resistance $3,925. Two-way risk at the print.

Backdrop: the market is ~94% priced for a 25bp Dec hike, yields past 5%, and the Fed chorus this week (Schmid, Collins, Jefferson) has been hawkish. Warsh's known line — AI productivity can ease inflation — is the one dovish surprise that could lift gold.
Flip: if Warsh says AI disinflation is real and a Dec hike isn't a done deal, lean BUY; if he backs further tightening or keeps 50bp talk alive, SELL pressure — watch $3,850 then $3,832.
Caution: the first minutes after the remarks are spike territory — no manual scalps into the print, per the standing rule.

event: Fed Chair Warsh Opening Remarks (AI forum, San Francisco)
headline: Warsh gave no rate signal — AI remarks were neutral for gold
body: No numbers — a speech, not data. Warsh said AI will have a 'significant impact' on the economy, from rising growth with broadly shared gains to higher unemployment and a slowdown if investment returns disappoint. The Fed is modelling the scenarios — illustrative, not predictions. His line: the Fed's role is 'neither advocacy nor opposition'.
Verdict: in line — no policy signal. He said nothing about the near-term outlook for rates or the economy, exactly as expected from opening remarks at a themed conference.

What it means for gold: neutral. No new reason to reprice the December hike — markets still ~92–94% priced for 25bp, 10-year yield above 5%. The hawkish backdrop (hot CPI, Waller/Schmid/Collins/Jefferson) is unchanged.
Gold's reaction: no clear move reported yet — gold was around $3,860–3,890 into the remarks (overnight low $3,832).
Levels: support $3,850, then $3,832; resistance $3,923, then $4,000. Next real triggers: US Retail Sales Tue 20:30 Phnom Penh, FOMC minutes Wed.
Call: NO TRADE — no rate signal, no fresh trigger; a trade here would be guessing, not trading the news.

headline: ADP weekly pulse in ~10 min — lagged average, no consensus, no trade into it
body: No forecast published — no consensus exists for this weekly pulse. Previous: 19.75K (4-week average, week ending 24 Oct).
This is a lagged 4-week moving average (data ~2 weeks old), not a fresh payroll count — it rarely moves gold on its own.
Gold ~$3,865, hovering near a 14-month low; day range $3,843–$3,887. Support $3,840–$3,845, resistance $3,880. A firm dollar and Fed-tightening bets keep it pinned.
The real mover tonight is US Retail Sales at 20:30 Phnom Penh (high impact) — just 15 minutes later. ADP is the warm-up, not the trade.
Flip: a jump in the average above ~25K would back the dollar and push gold toward $3,845 support; a drop below ~15K would ease dollar pressure and open $3,880.
Caution: the first minutes after a release are spike territory — no manual scalps into the print, per the standing rule.

headline: US Retail Sales in ~10 min — soft consensus already priced, gold pinned on $3,850 support
body: Forecast vs previous: headline +0.2% vs +0.8% in September; ex-autos +0.4% vs +0.9%; control group +0.4% vs +0.1%.
Gold ~$3,865, holding just above key $3,850 support (Monday's low $3,832.70). Resistance $3,880-3,890, then $3,900-3,920.
The consensus is already a sharp slowdown, so an in-line print is mostly priced in and changes little on its own.

A beat (+0.5% or more) would lift the dollar — already at a 19-month high near 103.6 — and December hike bets (~96-100% priced for 25bp) and push gold down; a miss (near 0% or a weak control group) would ease hike bets and let gold bounce.
Trend stays down: gold -6.5% in 20 days, below all major moving averages, 10-year yield above 5%. No edge in guessing long or short before the number.
Flip: beat of +0.5%+ with a strong control group -> SELL lean, $3,800 next; miss at 0.0% or below, or a falling control group -> BUY lean, $3,900-3,920 next.
Caution: the first minutes after a release are spike territory — no manual scalps into the print, per the standing rule.

headline: ADP jobs pulse beat the last print (24K vs 20K) — small, lagged, no trade
body: Actual: 24K average weekly gain vs previous 20K (last print 19.75K for the window ending 24 Oct). No forecast was published for this weekly pulse.
Verdict: a modest beat vs the previous window — private hiring picked up slightly, but this is a lagged 4-week moving average, not a fresh payroll count.
What it means for gold: slightly stronger jobs is a small dollar-positive, gold-negative nudge — but too small and too stale to move the market on its own.
Gold's reaction: no specific move reported on this print — gold was holding ~$3,855-3,865 around the release, just above the key $3,850 support (Monday's low $3,832.70).
Levels: support $3,850, then $3,832; resistance $3,880, then $3,895-3,900. The real test came 15 minutes later: US Retail Sales at 20:30 Phnom Penh.
Call: NO TRADE — a lagged average with no consensus is not a trading signal.

headline: Retail Sales in line on the headline, but the core beat — consumer still spending, no relief for gold
body: Actual: headline +0.2% MoM vs +0.2% forecast, previous +0.8%. Ex-autos +0.6% vs +0.4% forecast (beat). Control group +0.60% vs +0.10% previous — a strong beat. YoY +6.8% vs +6.3%.
Verdict: headline in line, core and control group beat — the US consumer is still spending, and spending is what feeds the December hike case.
What it means for gold: no relief — a resilient consumer keeps the December 25bp hike ~95-96% priced, the dollar near a 19-month high and the 10-year yield above 5%.
Gold's reaction: no specific post-print move reported yet in the wires — gold was ~$3,855-3,865 around the release, hugging the key $3,850 support after Monday's low of $3,832.70.
Levels: support $3,850, then $3,832, then $3,800. Resistance $3,880, then $3,895-3,900, then $3,920. A break below $3,832 opens $3,800; a reclaim of $3,900 would ease the pressure.

Call: NO TRADE — the headline was exactly in line, so there is no new edge to chase at a 14-month low. Caution: the first minutes after the print are spike territory — no manual scalps, per the standing rule.

headline: FOMC minutes in ~10 min — December hike ~96% priced, no trade into a 3-week-old text
body: No forecast — minutes, not data. The Oct 27–28 meeting held rates at 3.75–4.00% (10–2 vote; Cook and Hammack dissented, wanting a hike). Markets read the minutes for how many officials backed a December hike.
A December 25bp hike is already ~96% priced (CME FedWatch), with ~70% odds of another in January — the hawkish lean is largely in the price, so a hawkish text has limited downside room.
Minutes are a 3-week-old text record, not a number to beat or miss. Moves come from headline wording ('many' vs 'a few' on December) and are usually smaller and choppier than a data print.

Gold ~$3,865, pinned near 13-month lows (Monday's low $3,832), below all major moving averages with RSI ~38; the dollar is at 19-month highs above 103.5 and the 10-year yield is ~5.13%. Trend is down, but price is sitting on support — chasing either way into the print is poor risk.

Flip: minutes showing 'many' officials opposed a December hike, or worried about the labour market, turn it BUY toward $3,900; broad support for a December hike plus openness to more hikes in early 2027 turns it SELL — watch $3,850, then $3,832 and $3,820.
Caution: the first minutes after the release are spike territory — no manual scalps into the print, per the standing rule.

headline: Bailey speaks in ~10 min — gold below $3,800 at a one-year low, Fed story dominates
body: No forecast or previous — a speech, not a number.

Gold is sliding hard — about $3,790, down ~1.7% today, below $3,800 for the first time since September 2025 (a one-year low). The dollar is near 19-month highs and the US 10-year is around 5.1%. Support ~$3,760, resistance ~$3,880.
Gold's driver today is the Fed, not the BoE — markets price a ~96% chance of a December Fed hike, with the FOMC minutes due tonight (02:00 Phnom Penh). A BoE speech rarely moves gold directly.

Bailey just hiked to 4% on 5 Nov and warned another hike is likely unless the Middle East conflict is resolved. Hawkish tone firms sterling and eases the dollar a touch — mild gold support at best; cautious tone does the opposite. Either way it is second-order next to the Fed story.

Flip: a clear surprise from Bailey plus gold reclaiming $3,800 turns it a short-term BUY lean; a dovish turn pushing the dollar higher with gold breaking $3,760 support turns it SELL. Either setup forms after the print, not into it.
Caution: the first minutes after a release are spike territory — no manual scalps into the print, per the standing rule.

headline: Bailey's morning slot was a pre-recorded fireside chat in Seoul — no new rate signal; gold still sliding under $3,800 on the Fed/dollar story
body: Result: no new signal. Bailey's 14:30 appearance was a pre-recorded fireside chat at the accountants' congress in Seoul, not a policy speech — no new rate guidance in the wires, and the pound was steady near $1.32.
Gold's slide is the Fed/dollar story, not Bailey: spot around $3,770–$3,790, below $3,800 for the first time since September 2025 and down about 2% today.
The dollar is near 19-month highs (~103.6) and the 10-year is above 5%, with a December Fed hike about 95% priced.
Call: NO TRADE — no new information to trade on, and gold is sliding into tonight's FOMC minutes (Thu 02:00 Phnom Penh), the real event. Don't chase shorts at one-year lows into that print.
Levels to watch: support $3,760, then the $3,700s; resistance $3,800 (now overhead) and $3,880.
Next up: Bailey speaks again at 22:00 Phnom Penh (high impact) — his first chance to react to today's UK inflation numbers — and Lagarde at 21:25.

headline: Housing data due in ~13 min — forecasts point to a small starts rebound (1.25M) and softer permits (1.38M); gold already down ~2.6% to near one-year lows on the Fed/dollar story
body: Forecast vs previous: Housing Starts 1.25M expected (WSJ median, +2.4% MoM) vs 1.221M in September; Building Permits 1.38M expected (-1.4%) vs 1.40M.
Gold is around $3,750, down about 2.6% today and near its session low ($3,746) — its lowest in over a year — with support near $3,717 and resistance at $3,810–$3,835.
The driver is the Fed/dollar story, not housing: the dollar is at 19-month highs (~103.6), the 10-year is near 5.1%, and a December 25bp Fed hike is about 96% priced.
Housing starts and permits are medium-impact, second-tier data that rarely moves gold — and the real event tonight is the FOMC minutes at 02:00 Phnom Penh.
Call: NO TRADE — a beat would firm the dollar and yields slightly (bearish gold), a miss would soften them slightly (bullish), but the effect is small and symmetric, with no edge into the print.
What would flip it: a big surprise — starts well above 1.30M or below 1.15M — plus a clear dollar move. Otherwise wait for the FOMC minutes.
Caution: the first minutes after a release are spike territory — no manual scalps into the print.

headline: Mixed print: starts beat big (+9.9%), permits missed big (−7.4%) — no edge for gold.
body: Housing Starts: +9.9% MoM (1.31M annual rate) vs +2.4% forecast (1.25M); previous revised to −7.0% — a clear beat.
Building Permits: −7.4% MoM (1.29M) vs −1.7% forecast (1.38M); single-family permits −8.7%, weakest since COVID — a clear miss.
Verdict: mixed — the two halves cancel each other out, and permits (the forward-looking one) still show a weak pipeline.
Gold was ~$3,763 into the print near its 13-month low; no source tied a move to this release. The driver stays the Fed: Dec 25bp hike ~96% priced, DXY at 19-month highs, 10Y ~5.10%.
Call: NO TRADE — mixed data gives the dollar no clear direction, and a housing print won't turn gold's rate-driven slide below $3,800.
Levels to watch: support $3,757 (today's low), then $3,750; resistance $3,800, then $3,835–$3,860. Next event: FOMC minutes Thu 02:00 Phnom Penh.

headline: Pending home sales due in ~10 min — forecast a smaller fall (−2.1% vs −7.3%); gold at a 13-month low, Fed story dominates
body: Forecast vs previous: −2.1% MoM expected (consensus around −2.0%) vs −7.3% in September — a smaller fall, but sales are still at their slowest pace since 2010, with 30-year mortgage rates above 7%.
Gold is ~$3,763–3,779, down ~2% today at a fresh 13-month low below $3,800 (day low ~$3,757). Support $3,757, then $3,750; resistance $3,800, then $3,810–$3,835.

The driver is the Fed, not housing: DXY at 19-month highs (~103.8), the 10-year ~5.10%, and a December 25bp hike ~95% priced. Pending home sales is second-tier data that almost never moves gold on its own.
A beat (a smaller fall, or a rise) would slightly soften the dollar and could lift gold a touch; a miss would deepen the weak-housing story — either way the move, if any, is small and fades fast.
Flip: a big surprise either way (a rise, or a fall worse than −5%) together with gold breaking $3,800 or losing $3,750 — even then, wait for the move to settle rather than chase it.
Caution: the first minutes after a release are spike territory — no manual scalps into the print, per the standing rule. The real event tonight is the FOMC minutes, Thu 02:00 Phnom Penh.

headline: Pending home sales fell 4.7% MoM — a miss vs the -2.1% forecast, but a smaller fall than September's -7.3%.
body: Actual -4.7% MoM vs forecast -2.1% and previous -7.3%; year-on-year -16.7% (NAR, confirmed by WSJ).
Verdict: MISS — a bigger fall than expected, and a second straight record low for the index, though a smaller fall than September.
NAR's chief economist said October 'could mark the low point' as mortgage rates 'appear to have topped out' (30-year rates peaked near 7.4% in October).
Gold stayed ~$3,770-3,785 around the release, still ~2% down today at a 13-month low below $3,800; no source tied any gold move to the print.
Call NO TRADE: the print cuts both ways and housing rarely moves gold — today's slide is a rates/DXY story, with a Dec 25bp hike ~96% priced.
Levels to watch: support $3,757 / $3,750, then $3,715; resistance $3,800, then $3,832. Next: FOMC minutes, Thu 02:00 Phnom Penh.

headline: FOMC minutes due 02:00 Phnom Penh — Dec 25bp hike ~96% priced; gold at 13-month low ~$3,742
body: Minutes of the Fed's Oct 27–28 meeting release at 02:00 Phnom Penh. No forecast/previous — minutes are text, not a number.
The Fed held at 3.75–4.00% on Oct 28 in a 10–2 vote; Cook and Hammack dissented, wanting an immediate 25bp hike.
A December 25bp hike is ~96% priced (CME FedWatch), so the hawkish lean is largely in the price already.
Gold ~$3,742, below $3,800 at a 13-month low, down ~2.8% today; DXY at 19-month highs, 10Y ~5.1%. Support $3,717/$3,700, resistance $3,810–3,835 then $3,865.
What would flip the call: a dovish surprise (officials pushing back on a December hike) would favour BUY; broad support for a 50bp December hike would favour SELL.
Caution: the first minutes after a release are spike territory — no manual scalps into the print.
